Representatives of the AAP, Congress, BJP and SAD commended Chief Electoral Officer Anindita Mitra for transparency, consultation and addressing their concerns. Their endorsement comes amid protests against the Election Commission elsewhere, offering a striking contrast as Punjab’s voter list settles at just over 2.01 crore electors.

Ravichandran Ashwin emphasized that Bhuvneshwar concentrated on honing his skills instead of aiming for a comeback on the national team. Ashwin is optimistic about India's prospects in the upcoming 2027 ODI World Cup, attributing this to solid bowling assets and seasoned hitters. He pointed out South Africa's strength, citing their understanding of local conditions.

articles.title: Flydubai attack: UAE detains 2 Maldivian pilots over links with accused co-pilot - report
articles.summary: Authorities have detained two Maldivian pilots in connection with the flydubai stabbing incident that occurred recently. The stabbing incident involved Omani co-pilot Hammam al-Hammami attacking Indian pilot Smit Machchhar with an axe. Despite serious injuries, Machchhar managed to unlock the cockpit and stabilize the aircraft with crew assistance. Investigators are exploring al-Hammami's alleged extremist links and how he was hired by flydubai.

articles.title: US issues power grid emergency in 13 states: Reason and what it means for residents
articles.summary: In a decisive move to ensure grid stability during a peak demand period, US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright has empowered PJM Interconnection to manage local power generation units from October 13 to October 16. With temperatures hitting unseasonably high levels, demand has surged to approximately 111,500 megawatts on October 13. While residents are not required to take action, voluntary conservation measures may be recommended.

articles.title: Germany's Nuremberg Airport suspends flights after suspected aviation emergency
articles.summary: Nuremberg Airport experienced a temporary flight suspension after receiving reports of a suspected aviation emergency. Police confirmed the aircraft from Corfu landed safely amid the investigation. Eurofighter jets accompanied the plane, ensuring safety during the landing process. Additionally, there were earlier reports of a possible drone sighting near the airport, which authorities could not verify. This follows heightened concerns in Germany regarding drone incidents near critical infrastructure.

articles.title: ‘Not invited to party’: Bareilly teen stabbed repeatedly by neighbour, dies
articles.summary: In Gokulpur village, a 17-year-old boy named Arjun was fatally stabbed by his neighbor after a dispute. The disagreement arose when Vishal, who was allegedly drunk, was upset over not being invited to a birthday party. He confronted Arjun, who attempted to calm him down but was violently attacked instead. Angry villagers subsequently assaulted Vishal and locked him in a house until police arrived.

articles.title: Sensex ends 1,100 points higher, investors richer by Rs 4.12 lakh crore: Why markets are up today

Nifty50 closed at 22,721.95, up 359 points or 1.60%.The rally added more than Rs 4.12 lakh crore to the combined market capitalisation of listed companies, taking the total to Rs 470 lakh crore.

articles.title: No AC, yet naturally cool: Begum's 149-year-old palace now lies in ruins
articles.summary: Benazeer Palace, built in 1877, was once a symbol of architectural marvel and royal heritage. The palace features a unique cooling system using natural airflow and has many beautiful halls that remain intact. Despite undergoing restoration, it has not been effectively utilized and faces deterioration today. There was a proposal to transform it into a heritage hotel, though progress remains uncertain.

articles.title: Ben Affleck-backed initiative delivers 100m litres of clean water in Congo
articles.summary: In 2010, Ben Affleck established the Eastern Congo Initiative to foster development in the Democratic Republic of Congo. By 2024, this organization has provided over 100 million litres of clean water across various regions and facilitated access to essential health services for more than 400,000 individuals. The initiative’s social enterprise, Asili, is crucial in delivering sustainable services, showcasing the power of community-driven solutions in tackling humanitarian issues.

articles.title: Long Island’s 127-room Oheka Castle heads to auction with $63.5m debt
articles.summary: Oheka Castle, the largest residence on Long Island, will be auctioned on 27 October. The mansion, designed in 1919, is burdened with over $63.5 million in debt. Since its purchase in 1984, the current owner invested about $50 million in restoration efforts. The property also has development potential with approved plans for 95 luxury condominiums. Prospective buyers must provide a $750,000 deposit to participate in the auction.

articles.title: Sergey Brin is biggest donor against California wealth tax; could owe $13 billion

articles.title: Grand Canyon trout removal helps native fish populations rise over 400%
articles.summary: Historically, Bright Angel Creek was a sanctuary for various native fish species, including the endangered humpback chub. However, the rise of non-native brown trout has threatened this ecosystem. In an effort to restore balance, the Bright Angel Creek Trout Reduction Project was initiated, successfully eliminating invasive trout and leading to a remarkable 400% increase in native fish populations.

This revitalization forms part of the resort's centennial celebrations scheduled for 2026, with construction commencing the same year and concluding by 2029.

articles.title: Most Americans think Trump is profiting from presidency unethically or illegally
articles.summary: A recent poll revealed that a majority of Americans think Donald Trump is profiting illegally or unethically from his presidency. The survey indicated that around 60% of respondents believe Trump is prioritising personal financial interests over helping regular citizens. Financial disclosures suggested Trump has received significant investments in cryptocurrency ventures since returning to office. Concerns about Trump's financial conduct varied widely among political affiliations, with many Democrats alleging wrongdoing.

articles.title: Maharashtra man beats wife to death, walks into police station to confess

The couple had recently returned to Kannad town for the festive season. Following the incident, Kumbhakarna went to the local police station and confessed to the crime. Authorities have registered a murder case against him and an investigation is currently ongoing.

articles.title: Who is Neha Bora? Meet the JNUSU leader and AISA president

Ambedkar University and joined Jawaharlal Nehru University for PhD research in theatre and performance studies. Her journey from street theatre to activism includes a 23-day hunger strike and campaigns against examination centralisation.

articles.summary: Anduril Industries has unveiled the Steelfin family of surface-to-air interceptor missiles, specifically crafted to meet evolving air defense requirements. Their modular design allows for tailored configurations across diverse missions, streamlining production. Full-rate manufacturing is anticipated to commence by late 2028 or early 2029 following rigorous testing.

articles.title: Qatar Airways, travel portal ordered to pay Rs 3L after denying patient a ticket refund
articles.summary: A passenger was diagnosed with a brain tumour and had to cancel an international trip. He requested a refund from Qatar Airways and EaseMyTrip, providing medical documents. Despite his request, he was denied a refund and offered a reduced amount. The Hyderabad consumer commission found both companies responsible and ordered them to provide a full refund. The rover broke this record on October 11, during its 2,006th Martian day of the mission. Perseverance's autonomous navigation has been vital, accounting for over 90 percent of its driving distance. Additionally, it has discovered signs of ancient microbial activity and explored geological features within Jezero Crater.

articles.summary: Russia announced a one-day ceasefire to allow presidential elections in Ukraine, rejecting a longer truce proposed by Zelenskyy. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov emphasised the need for an overall peace deal instead of a temporary ceasefire. Zelenskyy suggested a 60-day ceasefire in response to criticism from Donald Trump regarding his leadership. He insisted that the decision about Ukraine's leadership belongs to its people and not external actors.

articles.title: Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar’s US Army job: Finding coders the Army doesn’t know it has
articles.summary: Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar, a lieutenant colonel in the US Army Reserve, told CBS News his main job is helping the Army find soldiers who can code. Working with the Army’s personnel department, he says skilled programmers in junior ranks have no clear career path. Sankar joined Detachment 201, the Army’s Executive Innovation Corps, in 2025 alongside Meta’s Andrew Bosworth and OpenAI veterans Kevin Weil and Bob McGrew.

Suraj Karkera expressed that the intense rivalry's absence will be missed but emphasized the team's focus on performance. The tournament is scheduled from October 27 to November 5 across Jalandhar and Mohali in Punjab.

articles.title: Retail inflation at almost 2-year high at 5.54%, driven by food prices surge
articles.summary: Retail inflation in India reached 5.54% in September, mainly spurred by rising food costs. Food inflation escalated to 7.74%, the highest recorded since the new CPI series was launched. The price of onions skyrocketed, while some items, like potatoes and tomatoes, saw price drops. Puducherry recorded the highest inflation rate at 6.86%, followed by Tamil Nadu.

articles.title: China’s secret women-only language is being revived by a new generation
articles.summary: Nüshu, an ancient script developed by women in Jiangyong County, China, served as a vital means of communication in a society dominated by men. Through this remarkable writing system, women conveyed their innermost thoughts and shared personal experiences. Although it nearly faded into obscurity, recent resurgence among young women and scholars has sparked new efforts for preservation, including national heritage recognition and artistic exploration to keep its legacy vibrant.

articles.title: 20k cops in schools, 80k edu institutions inspected as Poland tackles youth violence
articles.summary: Poland is deploying 20,000 police officers to educational institutions after three stabbings occurred within four days. Prime Minister Donald Tusk emphasised the alarming rise in violence among young people. Authorities connected some violent behaviour to content glorifying violence on the internet and in video games. Reports highlighted recent attacks, including one involving a 15-year-old. The government is committed to ensuring the safety of children in schools.

articles.title: 'He finds methods to score runs': Rahane highlights what makes Abhishek special

articles.title: Ohio protects 5,165 acres across 58 family farms from future development
articles.summary: Ohio has greenlit local sponsors to secure agricultural easements on 58 family-owned farms, aiming to safeguard farmland from non-agricultural development. Through the Local Agricultural Easement Purchase Program, farmers can keep cultivating their land while ensuring its preservation. Presently, more than 111,000 acres across 62 counties are safeguarded from development. With federal funding poised to enhance these efforts, local sponsors can apply for the 2027 program for further conservation.

articles.title: Brisbane family home held for 105 years sells for A$2.03 million
articles.summary: A 98-year-old woman in Brisbane, Australia, has sold a house built by her father in 1921 for A$2.03 million, ending 105 years of ownership by the same family. The three-bedroom property in Gordon Park attracted ten registered bidders, with five actively competing at auction. Several generations of the family were born in the house.

articles.title: New Jersey estate on 102 acres heads to auction with no minimum bid
articles.summary: On October 15, a stunning 26-acre estate located in Hopewell, New Jersey, will be auctioned off without a minimum bid requirement. The estate features a majestic main residence, a charming guesthouse, and recreational facilities such as a tennis court and a swimming pool. Furthermore, a vast 102-acre plot surrounds the estate, inviting potential buyers in a fluctuating luxury real estate landscape to engage in lively bidding.

articles.title: EC-SIR row: SC says it hasn't adjudicated on validity of new Form 6, will examine it
articles.summary: The Supreme Court addressed the controversy surrounding the new Form 6 used for voter registration. It clarified that it had not approved changes to the declaration regarding electoral rolls. The court's remarks arose during a hearing on the functioning of the Election Commission of India. Concerns were raised over the legality of the changes introduced in Form 6. The Supreme Court will further examine this issue in October.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo claims he's the greatest ever before reaching 1,000 goals
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo believes he is the greatest footballer ever, insisting his 980 career goals speak for themselves as he closes in on the 1,000-goal milestone. articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s Six Flags all set to sell many of its amusement parks as the company fights against lawsuits.

articles.title: Italian island school reopens for just one student after 20 years
articles.summary: In Ginostra, Italy, a six-year-old girl named Aysha is breaking new ground as she becomes the first student to attend the village's only school, which has reopened after two decades. Her family’s worries about their isolation on the island prompted this significant change. Lacking road access, the tight-knit community depends on boats for transportation, making the school’s revival crucial for future educational opportunities.

Economic Sciences Nobel 2026: Duo win for work on stability policy models
articles.summary: Robert E Hall and Michael Woodford received the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics from the Royal Swedish Academy. They were honoured for their work on macroeconomic stabilisation and developing important economic models. These models assist governments and central banks in managing economic fluctuations effectively. Their research highlighted decision-making processes of households and businesses, influencing fiscal and monetary policies.

articles.title: ‘We executed our plan against him’: Arshdeep on India's strategy to stop Shai Hope
articles.summary: India's bowlers effectively neutralised Shai Hope, sending him back to the pavilion for just five runs. articles.summary: Susan Downes, a retired general practitioner, is restoring a 200-hectare property for conservation in York. She has planted around 45,000 native seedlings and has managed to revive 45 plant species. In addition to restoration, Downes aims to create a conservation covenant for the land's future protection. Local volunteer groups and community members support her conservation efforts and engage in cultural activities.

articles.summary: A Connecticut town's plan to demolish a historic two-family home purchased for $455,000 to create around 20 parking spaces for a new library has faced opposition. articles.summary: A Frank Lloyd Wright-designed planetarium at Florida Southern College in Lakeland has reopened after more than 20 years of limited use. articles.title: 3 grades, 1 teacher: Haryana’s schools face a test
articles.summary: Haryana's education system is experiencing significant turmoil due to teacher shortages and administrative assignments disrupting classes. Government primary schools are struggling to function with only a few teachers managing multiple grades simultaneously. Many schools have reported that examinations cannot proceed effectively due to insufficient staff availability. Additionally, foundational learning assessments are failing to take place in numerous schools because of these staffing issues.

articles.title: How batting all-rounder Naman Dhir turned his bowling into a weapon for India
articles.summary: Naman Dhir, primarily recognised as a batting all-rounder, has made a significant impact with his bowling, particularly in a recent T20I match against the West Indies where he secured two important wickets. He attributes his bowling success to his keen understanding of batting techniques. While he still prioritises his batting skills, Dhir is dedicated to enhancing his bowling contributions, prioritizing enjoyment in his cricket journey.

articles.title: Australia removed rabbits; petrel colony grew to over 800 breeding pairs
articles.summary: After the successful elimination of rabbits from Cabbage Tree Island, conservationists observed a remarkable increase in the Gould’s petrel population. This pivotal action mitigated serious threats to their habitat and reproductive success, leading to over 800 breeding pairs by 2000, with annual offspring exceeding 400. To further bolster the species, a second breeding colony was initiated on Boondelbah Island, emphasizing the need for ongoing protective measures.

articles.title: Michael Dell’s Florida resort sells 40% of luxury condos, starting at $8.95m

The project represents a significant shift for a century-old resort previously focused on rental accommodations. Construction is expected to begin later this year, with completion anticipated in 2029.

articles.title: Bronze Age child burials reveal gender-linked funeral customs 4,000 years ago
articles.summary: The study of burial practices in Bronze Age Serbia indicates that children’s funerary treatment varied by biological sex, with research focused on two Maros culture cemeteries. Boys and girls were interred in contrasting ways, highlighting established gender roles. Interestingly, some burials challenged these customs, inviting reflection on societal standards. This work sheds light on the nuances of how ancient communities perceived and enacted gender distinctions in funerary rituals.

articles.title: Bill Gates-backed malaria nets helped fight disease, but are harming African waters
articles.summary: In various regions of Africa, the repurposing of insecticide-treated mosquito nets for fishing is becoming a growing trend. This alarming practice not only jeopardizes fish populations but also poses a serious threat to fragile aquatic ecosystems. Food-insecure families find this adaptation as a quick fix, but the harmful chemicals in the nets could also endanger marine life. A comprehensive strategy is essential to harmonize health measures with ecological integrity.

articles.title: Who was Madhu Kambikar? Veteran Marathi actress passes away at 73
articles.summary: Madhu Kambikar, a prominent figure in Marathi cinema, passed away on October 12 at the age of 73. She battled health issues, including a stroke in 2016 that left her bedridden for years. Kambikar appeared in over 75 films, becoming well-known for her roles in various Marathi productions. Her legacy also includes significant contributions to the classical art form of Lavani.

articles.title: Pakistan cricket hit by political turmoil! PCB shifts President’s Trophy matches

articles.summary: This week my colleague Antonio Regalado had an interesting update on GLP-1 weight-loss drugs. According to research presented at an aging meeting in Boston, these drugs seem to affect at least some measures of biological age. Overweight and diabetic people who take GLP-1s have a biological age around two to three years younger than similar…

articles.title: Starlink entry row: Is Ambani the real boss of India, asks Elon Musk
articles.summary: Elon Musk has raised concerns about regulatory obstacles facing Starlink's introduction in India. He claimed influential figures might be hindering the process and questioned if Ambani controls the situation. In response, India's government reaffirmed its fair and non-discriminatory approach, rejecting Musk's allegations. Other companies like Reliance Jio and Eutelsat OneWeb are also vying for approval to offer satellite services.

articles.title: 'Drunk men around me': Assam student's last video from train before she went missing
articles.summary: Himashri Boro, a 20-year-old student from Assam, was travelling alone after a dance competition. She felt unsafe in her train compartment due to inebriated men surrounding her and reached out to her family. Contact was lost between 2:30am and 3:00am, prompting her family to alert the railway authorities. Her body was later discovered near railway tracks in Andhra Pradesh’s Srikakulam district.

articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s presence puts Sanju Samson under pressure
articles.summary: Ishan Kishan is returning to his hometown of Ranchi, ready to take on the West Indies in the second T20I. This match offers a golden opportunity for Kishan to demonstrate his skill and confidence. The batting coach of India highlighted their unwavering fearless attitude towards the game. With selection decisions on bowlers and batting spots pending, players are eager to impress.

articles.title: 'This is emergency': 10,000 detained ahead of Delhi's Jantar Mantar stir, says CJP
articles.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party's planned protest in Delhi has faced significant opposition, leading to numerous detentions across the country. Over 10,000 individuals, including students, were detained ahead of the October 10 demonstration. CJP leaders have criticized the government's restrictions on public gatherings while demanding accountability for alleged electoral irregularities. As civil society groups rally in support, the party persists in organizing the protest.

articles.title: Anthropic updates Claude policy, may ‘ban’ users who are abusive or cruel to its AI
articles.summary: Anthropic has unveiled vital changes to its acceptable usage policy for the AI model Claude. These refined guidelines primarily aim to combat various forms of abuse directed at the AI and address new threats. Among the prohibitions are actions such as deception, interference with elections, and attempts to weaponize the AI. Furthermore, human supervision is now a mandatory requirement for all AI applications, ensuring safety and accountability in technology.

articles.title: Woman claims 2.5 acres was ancestral after stepmother sold it; why HC rejected plea
articles.summary: The Madras High Court held that the property was not ancestral but self-acquired. As a result, under Hindu law, the man and his mother were legally entitled to execute the gift settlement deed in favour of the man’s second wife, who could subsequently sell the property.

articles.title: Flydubai cockpit attack: Israel to honour Capt Smit with top civilian bravery award
articles.summary: Israel has announced that Captain Smit Machchhar will receive a prestigious Presidential Award for his bravery. He prevented a potential aviation disaster aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073 by acting decisively against a radicalized co-pilot. During the incident, six Israeli passengers displayed great courage in assisting Machchhar and foiling the hijack attempt. This heroic act has led to a broader investigation into the circumstances of the attack.

Along the journey, King and his team raised more than $766,000 and distributed funds to over 70 individuals and organisations, supporting families and communities facing financial hardships.

articles.title: Swift, Kelce called 'absentee' owners over $5.35M Ohio mansion plan
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are facing objections from neighbours over security fencing and landscaping at their $5.35 million Ohio mansion. Residents have raised concerns about a shared sewer line, wildlife safety and privacy. The couple’s representatives say they scaled back the fence and preserved neighbour access, while the board requested revisions to shoreline tree plans.

articles.title: Jaipur couple started with rented cows; now runs Rs 2.4 crore sustainable farm
articles.summary: Founded in 2018 by Vibhor Jain and Ishita Jain, Kinaya Organic Farms began with a handful of Gir cows. Fast forward to today, they operate a flourishing farm with 100 cows, branching into a variety of dairy products and agroforestry practices. Their sustainable approach incorporates cow dung biogas, rainwater management, and solar energy, ensuring a self-sufficient model that yields impressive annual profits while promoting environmental stewardship.

articles.title: Stock recommendations: Which stocks should you buy or sell on October 9?

Donna Kelce’s cookie fundraiser: How did she raise $4,100 for students?
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s mom Donna Kelce helped turn her famous family cookie recipe into a charity fundraiser for Kansas schoolchildren. After small-business owner Annie Stowe received permission to print the recipe on handmade mugs, $5 from each sale went towards paying elementary school lunch debt. The mugs initially raised $2,000 in 2023, followed by another $2,100 after local coverage, bringing the total to $4,100.

articles.title: Abhishek Sharma on the cusp of breaking Suryakumar Yadav’s unique T20I record
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma is on the brink of achieving a remarkable milestone, needing just 53 runs to cross 2,000 T20I runs during the second T20I against West Indies. With a chance to eclipse Suryakumar Yadav's record for the fastest attainment of this feat, Sharma's current high strike rate demonstrates his game-changing prowess.

articles.title: 'Ready to do everything in our power': Putin offers to help end Iran war
Branson bought $6m island for $100k to impress girl, now worth millions
articles.summary: Richard Branson was 29 when he pursued an island to impress Joan Templeman, offering $100,000 for a property priced at $6 million before eventually buying it for $180,000. In 2007, he purchased 125-acre Moskito Island for $15 million. Today, the island has been divided among nine private families who own estates there.

articles.title: Ontario man wins OHIP battle for US cancer therapy
articles.summary: Ontario man Alex Shved, who has Stage 4 melanoma, challenged OHIP after it denied funding for TIL therapy in Florida costing about US$600,000. A court ordered the province to reconsider his request. OHIP later rejected it again, while Ontario changed regulations governing out-of-country drug funding, limiting when patients can receive public coverage abroad.

articles.title: Mumbai CEO marks birthday with 90-hour fast, says he felt stronger
articles.summary: Abhishek Agarwal, a Mumbai-based CEO, completed a 90-hour fast to celebrate his birthday. This personal challenge was aimed at pushing his limits and testing his discipline. The experience transitioned from a physical test to a mental one as the days progressed. Responses to his LinkedIn post ranged from admiration to caution about prolonged fasting. The conversation sparked online includes reflections on personal limits and endurance.

articles.title: IAF celebrates its 94-year-old glorious journey
articles.summary: Indian Air Force celebrated its 94th anniversary at Hindon Air Force Station showcasing its historical significance. The event featured aerobatics by the vintage Tiger Moth and a display of military aircraft. IAF Chief ACM Singh emphasized the importance of operational preparedness and joint operations with the Army and Navy. PM Narendra Modi and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh commended the courage and dedication of IAF personnel.

articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's explosive net session raises big question: Will he play in Ranchi?
articles.summary: The young batter went on an attacking spree in the nets, repeatedly hitting the ball over the boundary and towards the stands. With every big hit, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi showed why he has become one of the most talked-about young batters in the Indian squad.

articles.title: GST Council scraps tax officers' arrest powers, eases refund rules
articles.summary: The GST Council has proposed major procedural changes to enhance business operations and tax compliance. These reforms aim to streamline registration, refunds, and input tax credit processes while lowering compliance costs. Additionally, the council will remove officers' powers for arrests under the GST framework. Processing of refunds will be expedited, with a goal to resolve claims within three days.

articles.title: ‘Krantiveer’ in life, ‘Natsamrat’ on screen: Nana dies at 75
articles.summary: Nana Patekar, a renowned actor from Maharashtra, passed away unexpectedly from a heart attack in Goa. He was known for his powerful performances in both Hindi and Marathi cinema, spanning nearly five decades. Patekar had a notable impact on Indian cinema, often portraying characters that were unpredictable and emotionally complex. He championed various social causes, including rural distress through his NAAM Foundation.

articles.title: 'Tell your story': Pat Cummins' blunt response to Khawaja's book on Sandpapergate
articles.summary: Australia captain Pat Cummins has played down concerns that Usman Khawaja’s upcoming autobiography could bring fresh attention to the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, also known as Sandpapergate. Australia are returning to South Africa for the first time since the scandal. The three-Test series begins at Kingsmead on Friday, but Cummins said the incident had already been dealt with and the team had moved on.

articles.title: Will those whose earnings have stopped love me: PM Modi amid SIR row
articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi called for a global effort to address cyber frauds and deepfakes at the India Mobile Congress. He highlighted the importance of mobile technology as a tool for governance and effective service delivery. Modi attributed significant financial savings to digital direct benefit transfers in India. He urged collaboration among governments and tech companies to enhance security measures in the telecom sector.

articles.title: ‘Reckless’ use of NSA has made it ordinary: MP HC
articles.summary: Madhya Pradesh high court quashed the preventive detention of two brothers under the National Security Act. The court criticized the reckless invocation of the Act by authorities and highlighted a lack of evidence. It found the brothers had been acquitted in multiple cases where NSA was applied, asserting non-application of mind. The court underscored the need for constitutional safeguards against arbitrary detentions.

articles.title: Nana Patekar death: Goa Police register 'unnatural death' case
articles.summary: Nana Patekar passed away due to a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa early Thursday morning. He was declared dead after attempts to revive him were unsuccessful at Manipal Hospital. The Goa Police have registered an 'Unnatural Death' case to investigate the circumstances surrounding his death. A post-mortem examination is being conducted to ascertain the exact cause of death.

articles.title: AI use ups homework scores, but slashes exam marks: Study
articles.summary: World Bank's report reveals that unrestricted use of generative AI may enhance homework scores while diminishing actual learning outcomes. Evidence indicates that students using AI showed improvement in assignments but performed worse in exams over time. Concerns exist regarding students outsourcing their learning process to AI rather than engaging in cognitive effort. However, AI used by teachers to customize instruction shows promising learning gains.

articles.title: KPSC scam candidates taken to resorts, provided with Q&A: ED
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate reported on a significant corruption case involving the Karnataka Public Service Commission. Candidates for the veterinary officers' exam were allegedly bribed to receive leaked test papers before the exam. An organized syndicate was involved in the manipulation of the recruitment process, leading to multiple arrests of officials. Investigations revealed a systematic approach to generating proceeds of crime through examination material leaks.

articles.title: Group of 42 ex-judges defends SIR, slams opposition attack on Election Commission
articles.summary: A group of 42 retired judges has expressed concerns over criticism directed at the Election Commission. They stated these attacks serve vested political interests, compromising democratic integrity. The judges defended the EC's actions as essential to maintaining clean electoral rolls for fair elections. They urged political parties to present legit grievances formally, rather than delegitimizing the electoral process.

articles.title: Jharkhand should 'revisit' DGP appointment rules, says Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stated that the appointment process for Jharkhand's DGP likely violated its previous judgment regarding officer tenure. The court issued a notice to Tadasha Singh, appointed shortly before her retirement. The Central Government argued that Jharkhand's amended regulations overstepped the Supreme Court's mandate on DGP appointments. Jharkhand, represented by Kapil Sibal, criticized the selective enforcement of these regulations by the Centre.

articles.title: IPS quota in CAPF posts comes into force
articles.summary: The Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026, has come into effect on October 8. This Act mandates that senior posts in CAPFs be filled by IPS officers on deputation. The government supports this move for better coordination between the Centre and states. CAPF cadre officers express concerns regarding career advancement due to this new quota.

articles.title: Proof of 21 'compromised transfers', 11 policy changes part of CBI's Punjab file
articles.summary: CBI has obtained evidence related to compromised transfers involving 21 senior officials in Punjab government and police. The probe focuses on a cash-for-postings scam connected to OSD to Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann. Allegations include various requests for administrative favors and transfer requests surrounding certain officers. The investigation involves interactions with individuals linked to tender manipulations across the state.

articles.title: J&K: High court orders passport revival for student purusing MBBS in Iran
articles.summary: Ibra Khan, a student pursuing MBBS at Tehran University, had her passport impounded due to her father's past case. The Jammu & Kashmir High Court intervened, recognizing her completion of half the course before the impounding occurred. Legal representatives argued that Khan could not be held accountable for her father's actions from 1997. A division bench ordered the passport's revival while allowing authorities to impose conditions on its use.

articles.title: Cancer drug prices may fall as government plans 30% trade margin cap
articles.summary: The Indian government has announced plans to cap trade margins on all types of cancer drugs. This decision aims to make cancer medications more affordable and accessible, potentially reducing prices by up to 70%. It is expected to result in savings of around Rs 2,500 crore annually for patients. An expert committee will be formed to recommend the list of drugs covered by this initiative.

articles.title: Defence secy talks to German envoy & Greece dy min to widen strategic partnerships
articles.summary: Newly appointed German Ambassador Jasper Wieck met with Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh to discuss defense cooperation. India and Germany aim to strengthen their military and defense-industrial ties, including advanced technologies. The talk follows high-level engagements and a recent agreement on co-development of defense items. Meanwhile, India engages with Greece on maritime security and coastal protection issues.

Its combat record spans the Second World War, the wars of 1947-48, 1965 and 1971, Kargil, Balakot and Operation Sindoor. The force is now evolving into a networked aerospace power, built around the Integrated Air Command and Control System, growing unmanned capabilities and long-range airlift. The building reportedly belonged to the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board and was around 20-25 years old.

articles.title: Man beheads minor girlfriend in forest, dies in crash while fleeing
articles.summary: A 17-year-old girl was reported missing and found murdered in a forest in Madhya Pradesh. Ankit Malviya, her boyfriend, allegedly killed her after an argument, using a saw. He later called his cousin to confess before attempting suicide and colliding with a truck. Police discovered the girl's body and a saw at the scene, along with a rope noose.

articles.title: 'Unko select karke koi meherbani nahi ki': Wasim on Bhuvneshwar's India return
articles.summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to India’s T20I squad has received strong backing from former India batter Wasim Jaffer, who believes the experienced pacer’s selection is based on his performances and fitness, rather than any favour. Bhuvneshwar, 36, has been recalled for India’s five-match T20I series against New Zealand, beginning October 22. Jaffer feels the veteran seamer should have been brought back into the national setup earlier.

articles.title: Some oligarchs blocking entry of Starlink in India: Elon Musk
articles.summary: Elon Musk has claimed that certain oligarchs are obstructing Starlink's entry into the Indian market. Starlink has already established the necessary infrastructure and is prepared to launch its services. The company aims to provide affordable broadband connectivity to areas lacking internet access. Regulatory approvals are awaited before the commercial rollout can commence in India. Collaboration with local telecom operators has been a key element in Starlink's strategy for success.

articles.title: HubSpot, one of the UK's biggest technology companies, is cutting hundreds of jobs
articles.summary: In a significant move, HubSpot, a leading technology firm based in the UK, will cut around 660 jobs as part of a strategic overhaul to better integrate AI advancements. CEO Yamini Rangan discussed three pivotal changes aimed at improving customer experiences and optimizing management. Employees losing their positions will be provided with severance and support during the transition, highlighting a shift in the company’s focus and strategies.

articles.title: 'Stabbed 7 times': How bid to seal petrol pump turned deadly for IndianOil official
articles.summary: In a tragic incident, Mahesh Shelke, the sales manager for IndianOil, was fatally stabbed during an altercation at a petrol pump as he sought to take control of the outlet amid a dispute. Swift action was taken by authorities, resulting in the arrest of five individuals, including members of the Pandavveer family. IndianOil and the petroleum ministry have rallied to support Shelke's family during this devastating period.

articles.title: US-based woman files case against parents for property share; Karnataka HC rejects it
articles.summary: The case involves a dispute over whether properties that had come to the woman’s father from her grandfather retained the character of ancestral property, giving her a right to seek partition under the Hindu Succession Act. The woman, based in the US, has been living abroad since her marriage in 1979. She filed a suit seeking partition of family properties and an equal share in them after her father sold one property.

articles.title: US to strike Iran? Pentagon orders military to gear up for attacks
articles.summary: The Pentagon has been instructed to prepare for possible military actions against Iran, amid stalled diplomatic efforts. Preparations may lead to attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities and strategic sites, although no attack timeline has been set. This situation overlaps with renewed fighting in Yemen, where Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have intensified. Meanwhile, elections in the US and Israel may influence military decisions in the region.

articles.title: Delhi Police likely to file FIR over alleged assault on police during Congress protest
articles.summary: Delhi Police is reviewing videos to identify protesters involved in the alleged assault during a Congress protest. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi were detained for defying police orders while attempting to proceed to Jantar Mantar. Police are also taking action against misleading social media posts regarding their conduct during the protest. Earlier, an FIR was lodged against Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi for forcibly entering Akashvani Bhawan.

articles.title: Texas carries out first US execution since Christa Pike's botched lethal injection
Swiss solar panels on railway tracks survive 11,000 trains, generate 16,000 kWh
articles.summary: In 2025, Swiss startup Sun-Ways installed 48 removable solar panels across 100 metres of active railway tracks in Buttes. More than 11,000 trains have since passed over the installation, which has generated over 16,000 kWh of electricity. The three-year pilot is testing whether unused railway space can safely produce renewable energy without disrupting operations.

articles.title: Northern lights may light up US, Canada tonight amid G1-G2 storm
articles.summary: Northern lights may return across parts of the US and Canada overnight October 8-9 as a CME reaches Earth after an M1.4 solar flare. NOAA forecasts G1 to G2 geomagnetic storm conditions, with activity potentially strengthening early Friday. Alaska, Canada and northern US states have the best viewing chances under dark skies.

articles.title: Why some kids line up toys instead of playing, per psychology
articles.summary: Young children often engage in repetitive activities, like lining up their toys, to make sense of their surroundings. This might appear peculiar at first glance; however, it serves as a valuable learning process. Parents should take note of their child's responses when changes occur in their play setup. If a child seems particularly upset, it may signal the need for a deeper developmental assessment.

articles.title: 'Naman Dhir has finished him': World Cup winner's big statement on star's T20I future
articles.summary: Naman Dhir had scored 318 runs in IPL 2026 but did not bowl a single over during the tournament. His international debut showed that he can offer India another option with the ball. Former India cricketer and 1983 World Cup winner Krishnamachari Srikkanth believes Dhir’s emergence could seriously hurt Washington Sundar’s chances in white-ball cricket.

articles.title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ $1.6m philanthropy: How are they helping 20,000 kids?
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have made children a major focus of their charitable work through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation. Their efforts include a $1.625 million Boys & Girls Clubs commitment, a $1 million inclusive Kansas City playground, literacy programs reaching more than 20,000 students, community grants and food support for families facing hardship.

articles.title: IIT-B puts on hold 2026 rules on tough penalties for cheating
articles.summary: IIT-Bombay’s senate has halted new penalties for academic misconduct, reverting to the 2015 policy for upcoming examinations. This decision follows the recent death of a student suspected of cheating during an exam. An interim procedure allows faculty to document suspected dishonesty while encouraging student accounts on a separate form. Faculty members and students will present their cases before a disciplinary committee after the examination period.

articles.title: Oil remains beyond $100 per barrel as Middle East supply concerns persist
articles.summary: As tensions escalate in the Middle East, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz, oil prices have surged amid fears of potential supply disruptions. Recent assaults on tankers heighten the danger of transporting crude through this vital corridor. Additionally, American crude inventories are dwindling, signaling a tighter market, while diesel and jet fuel stocks remain below average levels, a trend seen for over seven months since the onset of regional conflict.

articles.title: Russia rejects second plague scare as WHO demands answers over Siberian lab deaths
articles.summary: In response to concerns over a second suspected plague case linked to a worker's death, Russia has denied these allegations. The World Health Organization is looking for more details on the illness that led to the worker's pneumonia. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov denounced many media reports as false. Health officials assure the public that there is no epidemic threat while WHO seeks more information to evaluate health risks.

articles.title: 'We'll do it': PM Modi gives slogan for 2047 goals
articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi delivered a speech highlighting his 25 years in government and the goal of developed India by 2047. He called upon citizens to commit to this ambitious target and emphasized the power of the people. Modi reiterated the importance of extraordinary goals, linking good governance to societal inclusion. He reflected on his journey from humble beginnings to leadership in the BJP.

articles.title: 'Satisfied with my runs': Pakistan batter opens up on Asian Games final loss to India
articles.summary: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to win the men’s cricket gold medal at the Asian Games last week.

articles.title: India's diabetes burden is creating another problem: The growing threat to eyesight
articles.summary: Diabetic retinopathy often progresses quietly, leading to significant eye damage before symptoms are detected. Therefore, routine eye exams are imperative for early identification, even if one's vision appears normal. Studies show a strong link between how long a person has diabetes and their risk of developing vision issues. Consistently managing blood sugar levels and health can help avert major vision loss.

articles.title: 'Fight goes on’: 87-yr-old woman dies after becoming symbol of Spain housing crisis
articles.summary: María del Carmen Abascal, known as Maricarmen, died in a hospital after being evicted from her home. Her eviction triggered nationwide protests highlighting the housing crisis afflicting Spain. Activists voiced anger over Maricarmen's death as a symbol of the struggle against rising rents and evictions. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez offered condolences, acknowledging the impact of her case on public sentiment.

articles.title: Loans set to get dearer as RBI hikes repo rate after 44 months
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has announced a 25 basis points increase in the repo rate to 5.5%. This decision reflects growing inflation pressures and stronger than anticipated economic growth. The rise in interest rates will lead to higher loan EMIs, impacting consumption during the festive season. Banks are expected to increase fixed deposit rates following this policy change.

articles.title: Anti-CEC protests: Oppn, police face off again; Rahul says won’t stop till Gyanesh quits
articles.summary: Opposition members from the INDIA bloc attempted to stage a protest demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. They were detained by Delhi Police less than a kilometer from their protest site at Jantar Mantar. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge organized the lunch gathering, where the protest plan was discussed. Difficulties in moving their buses led to further confrontations with police as they sought to demonstrate.

articles.title: 'Drishyam 3' Day 6: Ajay Devgn's film earns Rs 15.50cr, India total hits Rs 232.50cr
articles.summary: Ajay Devgn's film 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' continues to perform strongly at the box office. It recorded earnings of Rs 15.50 cr on its sixth day, accumulating a total of Rs 232.50 cr net in India. The movie, which opened with Rs 62.00 cr, has reached a worldwide gross of Rs 366.50 cr. Its performance over six days led to over 9.5 million footfalls globally.

articles.title: Living Planet Report: WWF finds 73% global wildlife decline; India shows recovery gains
articles.summary: A global decline of 73% in monitored wildlife populations occurred between 1970 and 2022. India has successfully improved populations of tigers, one-horned rhinos, and Ganga river dolphins. The report highlights threats like habitat loss, climate change, and pollution affecting wildlife. Despite the negative trends, about half of monitored populations are stable or increasing globally. Targeted conservation efforts in India demonstrate the potential for wildlife recovery and biodiversity preservation.

articles.title: Proselytising organisations can’t get FCRA registration: Madras HC
Doctors, hospitals can't use AI to create testimonials: National Medical Commission
articles.summary: National Medical Commission has issued guidelines restricting the use of AI in medical advertising and patient testimonials. Registered medical practitioners and hospitals must not engage in creating synthetic content or manipulating search rankings. Claims of being the best or offering guaranteed results are also prohibited under these rules. Additionally, offering discounts or referrals that encourage unnecessary consultations is not allowed.

articles.title: Make a good film, repay your debts: Supreme Court to Rajpal Yadav
articles.summary: Supreme Court has maintained the condition for Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 2 crore for his appeal. Yadav took a loan of Rs 5 crore in 2010 for a film that never completed, which has accrued interest. His counsel mentioned he secured Rs 1.15 crore and aims to sell property to cover remaining dues. The court suggested producing a successful film may help him repay the debts.

articles.title: Assam CM Himanta Sarma says woman sent to Bangladesh safe, son counters CM
articles.summary: Mumtaz Begum, a woman expelled to Bangladesh, remains untraceable by her family despite official claims of her safety. Her son, Momruz Ali, is pleading for government assistance to locate her in either country. The Gauhati High Court directed authorities to find Mumtaz and provide interim compensation to her husband. Reports indicate that searches in Bangladesh yielded no results for her whereabouts so far.

articles.title: Mamata Banerjee’s Delhi arrival fuels buzz over INDIA bloc meet with President
articles.summary: TMC chairperson Mamata Banerjee's arrival in Delhi has heightened anticipation for the requested meeting with President Droupadi Murmu. The opposition bloc is awaiting confirmation for a meeting date between October 7 and 9. The delegation has been limited to ten members as requested by the President's Secretariat. CPI(M)'s John Brittas has submitted a petition for constitutional intervention regarding the Election Commission.

articles.title: With PM Modi set to visit Ottawa, India & Canada back CEPA
articles.summary: India and Canada are currently engaged in the fifth round of talks for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. Both countries aim to sign the CEPA during Prime Minister Modi's anticipated visit to Canada. The visit is tentatively scheduled for December 11-13, just before the G20 summit in Florida. Leaders from both nations envision boosting bilateral trade to CAD 70 billion by 2030.

articles.title: Centre cites Supreme Court order, seeks to void Jharkhand DGP appointment
articles.summary: Supreme Court has agreed to hear the application from the Centre regarding Tadasha Mishra's appointment as Jharkhand DGP. The appointment has been challenged due to its conflict with procedures set in the SC's 2006 Prakash Singh judgement. Moreover, the Centre claimed that prior DGP appointments in Jharkhand were also illegal for similar reasons. Mishra's appointment occurred shortly before her retirement, which raised legal concerns.

articles.title: Medical trips costliest in both rural & urban areas
articles.summary: Health and medical trips incurred the highest expenses in rural and urban areas during a one-year period. The average expenditure for these trips was notably higher in urban than rural areas. Pilgrimage travel accounted for the largest share of trips taken throughout the year. Accommodation and transport were significant expenditures for health and medical trips, underscoring their financial impact.

articles.title: 'Cash-for transfers' WA chats part of CBI dossier on Mann OSD
articles.summary: A set of WhatsApp chats has emerged, alleging monetary transactions involving senior Punjab government officials and DSPs. CBI's dossier includes these chats as they prepare to interrogate CM Bhagwant Mann's OSD Rajbir Singh Ghuman. Allegations suggest that intermediaries received bribes for influencing transfers and policy formulations affecting IAS and IPS officers. Additionally, documents indicate potential irregularities in real estate projects and the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority.

articles.title: 'One student, one day': CUET-UG 2027 may get shorter, simpler
articles.summary: CUET-UG 2027 may implement notable changes to streamline the examination experience for students. Candidates could see a reduction in the number of subjects from five to four over time. The proposed changes also include shortening the duration of individual papers to enhance efficiency. Subject grouping may allow related papers to be scheduled together for a single-day examination.

articles.summary: Inspectors of homoeopathic medicines must hold the appropriate qualifications, an industry body said, adding that domain expertise enables better guidance for manufacturers and pharmacists.

articles.summary: Cotton yarn prices have surged around 60%, from about  ₹250 per kg in early 2026 to nearly  ₹400 per kg now, putting pressure on textile manufacturers, particularly those that use yarn to produce fabrics and garments, per the industry proposal submitted to the textiles ministry and reviewed by Mint.
